results.name: One Arm Reverse Dumbbell Fly
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in one hand with a neutral grip. Bend at the hips and knees, keeping your back straight and almost parallel to the floor, and extend your free hand to hold on a bench.
Allow the dumbbell to hang straight down from your shoulder, with your arm fully extended towards the floor.
Raise the dumbbell out to the side until your arm is parallel to the floor, keeping a slight bend in your elbow.
Lower the dumbbell back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.
tips: Use a controlled motion to lift and lower the dumbbell, avoiding momentum.
Focus on using your shoulder muscles to lift the weight rather than swinging your arm.
Keep a slight bend in your elbow throughout the exercise to reduce strain on your joints.
results.description: One Arm Reverse Dumbbell Fly is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Overhand Clap
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms extended down to your sides, palms facing your torso.
Lift your arms overhead, bringing your palms together in a clapping motion.
Lower your arms back to the starting position with control, keeping them straight and at shoulder height.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining a smooth and controlled motion.
tips: Focus on steady breathing, inhaling as you lift your arms and exhaling as you lower them.
Ensure your shoulders stay relaxed and away from your ears to avoid unnecessary tension.
Keep your movements smooth and controlled and avoid using momentum.
results.description: Overhand Clap is an advanced single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Palm Up Palm Down Rotation
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms extended straight at your sides at shoulder height.
Slowly rotate your forearms in the opposite direction so that your palms face up while slightly lowering your arms.
Slowly raise your arms back to the starting position while rotating your forearms so that both palms face down.
Repeat for the desired repetitions.
tips: Focus on steady breathing, exhaling as you lower your arms and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and away from your ears to avoid unnecessary tension.
Maintain a slight bend in your elbows to reduce strain on your joints.
results.description: Palm Up Palm Down Rotation is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Plank Reverse Fly With Bottle
instructions: Start in a high plank position with your hands placed directly under your shoulders and your body forming a straight line from head to heels. Hold a water bottle in your right hand, and keep your feet slightly wider than hip-width apart for stability.
Lift the water bottle out to the side while keeping your arm straight, raising it until it is parallel to the floor.
Slowly lower the bottle back to the starting position with control.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your core engaged to maintain a stable plank position and prevent your hips from sagging or rotating.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and avoid using momentum.
Keep your arm straight and avoid locking your elbow to protect your joint.
results.description: Plank Reverse Fly With Bottle is an intermediate single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Lower Back.

results.name: Plate Car Driver
instructions: Stand holding a weight plate at the 3 and 9 o'clock positions, arms extended at shoulder height.
Turn the plate to one side as if steering a car.
Return to the centre and turn it to the other side.
Keep alternating while your arms stay at shoulder height.
tips: Keep your arms straight and level.
Keep your torso still.
results.description: Plate Car Driver is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Core.

results.name: Plate Front Raise
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a weight plate with both hands. Keep your arms extended straight down in front of your hips.
Raise the plate in front of you with straight arms until they are parallel to the floor, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the plate back to the starting position with control.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining good form throughout.
tips: Avoid using momentum to lift the plate; focus on a slow and controlled movement.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows to protect your joints.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you lift the plate and inhaling as you lower it.
results.description: Plate Front Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Plate Full Front Raise
instructions: Stand holding a weight plate at the sides, arms extended in front of your thighs.
Raise the plate in front of you with straight arms.
Continue up until it is overhead.
Lower slowly to your thighs and repeat.
tips: Brace your core so you don't lean back.
Use a light plate for the full range.
results.description: Plate Full Front Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Chest, Traps.

results.name: Plate Halo
instructions: Hold a weight plate by its sides in front of your chest.
Move the plate around your head in a circle, close to your head.
Bring it back to the front.
Repeat in one direction, then switch direction.
tips: Keep your core braced and hips still.
Keep the plate close to your head.
results.description: Plate Halo is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Upper Back, Core.

results.name: Plate Internally Rotated Rear Delt Fly
instructions: Hinge forward with a flat back, holding a light plate in each hand, thumbs turned in.
Let your arms hang below your shoulders.
Raise your arms out to the sides, leading with your elbows.
Lower slowly and repeat.
tips: Use light plates.
Squeeze your rear shoulders at the top.
results.description: Plate Internally Rotated Rear Delt Fly is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Traps.

results.name: Plate Lateral Raise
instructions: Stand holding a light weight plate in each hand at your sides.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows.
Raise your arms out to the sides until they reach shoulder height.
Lower slowly and repeat.
tips: Lead with your elbows.
Don't shrug your shoulders.
results.description: Plate Lateral Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Traps.
